quote: Beweise den folgenden Satz: Wenn ein Existenzbeweis in der Math. geführt worden ist, so ist stets auch die Construktion (durch endliche Zahl von Schritten, wie man zu sagen pflegt), ob ... möglich.
english: Prove the following theorem: If an existence proof has been carried out in mathematics, then the construction (by a finite number of steps, as one usually says) is also always possible, whether ...
topic: Philosophical notes on the relation of thought and reality, a proposed theorem that existence proofs imply constructibility, a question about perpetual motion of the second kind in living beings, the role of mathematics and the axiomatic method, and the beginning of a remark on experiments and geometry.

triage.modern_statement: Hilbert's proposed metatheorem: whenever an object is proved (classically) to exist, there is also an effective construction of it, meaning an algorithm with finitely many steps. In modern terms it reads: if a theory T proves ∃x φ(x), then some explicitly computable witness t satisfies φ(t). Equivalently, every classical existence theorem has a constructive or computable counterpart. The note breaks off at 'ob ...', so the exact scope Hilbert meant is uncertain.
triage.answered_by: The general claim was refuted, in the negative, by computability theory: Turing (1936–37) and Specker (1949) showed it fails. Specker built a computable, monotone, bounded sequence of rationals whose limit exists (by the monotone convergence theorem) but is not a computable real. Brouwer's intuitionism and later constructive mathematics treat the gap between classical existence proofs and constructions as basic and permanent. Hilbert's own basis theorem (1890) is the standard first example of a non-constructive existence proof.

evidence.claim: In 1949 Specker took up Turing's ideas on computable reals and constructed a computable monotone bounded sequence whose limit is not computable, establishing Turing's claim.

Turing 1937 / Specker 1949: there is a computable, monotone increasing, bounded sequence of reals whose supremum is not computable. The monotone convergence theorem therefore has no computable version.
The Hilbert Basis Theorem was the first major non-constructive proof recognized in mathematics (Gordan: 'das ist keine Mathematik, das ist Theologie').
Constructive mathematics (the BHK interpretation) holds that an existence proof by contradiction does not give a construction. Hilbert's deep existence theorems are named as examples.
Non-constructive existence proofs, including Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and basis theorem, are distinguished from constructive proofs.

triage.why: The sources show that classical existence does not, in general, imply effective constructibility: Specker's sequence has a limit that provably exists but cannot be computed. That answers the general form of Hilbert's proposed theorem in the negative. It is not one of the 23 Problems, though it is close to Hilbert's 'no ignorabimus' optimism and his later finitist program. The question of which existence theorems do have constructive or computable content is still actively studied, in constructive and computable analysis, reverse mathematics and proof mining. Confidence is medium for three reasons: the note is cut off at 'ob ...', the page is undated, and none of the sources mention this diary entry, so linking it to these results is my own reading.
